messages.body_plain:
Yes, it isn't a great design decision. the values and keys are
contained in the R vectors
map.values and map.keys. rhipe_map_buff_size is the length of the of
these vectors.
So if the input format is  'text', this means that map.values will
contain map_buff_size number of lines.

In the airline example, this means that the the map.values will
contain rhipe_map_buff_size number of
data frames (each of which were several thousands of rows) - this is
why in the airline (some of them)
i specify rhipe_map_buff_size a small number because when the text
input was saved as data frames,
the entire map.values (default is 5000 lines of text ) is saved as a data frame.

So if one reads this source, it isn't a good idea to allow the length
of map.values to have the default length -that implis
5000 data frames of 5000 rows each. It's better to set
rhipe_map_buff_size to something like 5-10.

That the user has to think about the size of rhipe_map_buff_size is  bad design.

Regards
J

reducer (cannot use map file anymore)

There are several ways.

1. For a large number of variables (or large in size e.g. a few MB)

rhsave(n1,n2,n3, file="/path-on-hdfs/data.Rdata")

map.setup = expression({
   load("data.Rdata") # no need to give full path
})

rhmr(...,setup=list(map=map.setup),
shared.files=c("/path-on-hdfs/data.Rdata"),....

2. Serialize as strings and pass via mapred

mapred=list()
mapred$c1 = rawToChar(serialize(c1,NULL,ascii=TRUE))
mapred$c2 = rawToChar(serialize(c2,NULL,ascii=TRUE))

map.setup = expression({
    c1 = unserialize( charToRaw( Sys.getenv("c1") ))
    c2 = unserialize( charToRaw( Sys.getenv("c2") ))
})

rhmr(,.., mapred=mapred,setup=list(map=map.setup))

3. Modify R code using bquote (you should be comfortable with
modifying code at run time)

map = as.expression(bquote({
            c1 <- .(c1)
            c2  <- .(c2)
    .....}, list(c1=c1,c2=c2)))

rhmr(map=map,...)

Note, this code is parsed and modified before being sent to Hadoop. c1
and c2 are hardcoded into the source. Try this

c1=matrix(runif(10),ncol=2)
c2=matrix(runif(10),ncol=2)
map = as.expression(bquote({
            c1 <- .(c1)
            c2  <- .(c2)
    }, list(c1=c1,c2=c2)))

and type map, you'll see c1 and c2 in the source. Use this for i)
small number of global variables ii) small sized variables (< MB)

You did download Rhipe from the website [1] ?
Also, the following worked for me:

map <- expression({
  lapply(map.values,function(seed){
    set.seed(seed)
    numDraws <- 1e2
    r <- .5 #radius... in case the unit circle is too boring
    x <- runif(numDraws, min=-r, max=r)
    y <- runif(numDraws, min=-r, max=r)
    inCircle <- ifelse( (x^2 + y^2)^.5 < r , 1, 0)
    rhcollect(1,sum(inCircle) / length(inCircle) * 4)
  })
})

Hi,

So your error is

Error in split.default(seq_len(nrow(x)), f, drop = drop, ...) :
> >  Group length is 0 but data length > 0

but mine is something to do  with a vector. Anyways, it appears the
split function in the map might be causing it.

So, remove the reduce (we don't need it - the data wont get to the reduce, the
job will fail before it can).

And rewrite the map to look like

map <- expression({
  h <- do.call("rbind",map.values)
  d <- h[h$carrier=='WN',,drop=FALSE]

  tryCatch({

    if(nrow(d)>0){
      e <- split(d,list(d$year,d$month,d$mday))
      lapply(e,function(r){
        k <- as.vector(unlist(r[1,c("year","month","mday")]))  ##
remove attributes
        rhcollect(k, r)
      })
    }

  },error=function(er) {
    rhcounter("err",er,1)
    rhcollect("error",list(er,d))
  }
           )
})

Notice that this block

   if(nrow(d)>0){
      e <- split(d,list(d$year,d$month,d$mday))
      lapply(e,function(r){
        k <- as.vector(unlist(r[1,c("year","month","mday")]))  ##
remove attributes
        rhcollect(k, r)
      })
    }

is wrapped in tryCatch and if an error happens the we catch it in the 'error'
parameter.  Instead of failing the job, we write the error message and the data
'd'.  (It could be possible to fail the job - you could save the offending
objects to a unique filename on the HDFS).

Now lets read one error (btw, it is possible that not all key-values correspond
to errors, if errors are few you might want another mapreduce on the output to
subset error kv pairs or dont even use rhcollect(k,r) (in above code)).

x <-  rhread("/tmp/southwest",type='map',max=1)
h <- x[[1]][[2]][[2]]

Now stepping through the above code, the line

 e <- split(d,list(d$year,d$month,d$mday))

is the offender and that's because d does not have the column mday (my
typo). So replace mday with 'day' (everywhere) and try again.

What version of R are you using? My error was different, but i guess it's the
same cause.

Cheers
Joy
